sk-9947b15d.stem: The xiphoid process most often corresponds to which vertebral level?
sk-9947b15d.explanation: The xiphisternal joint lies at about the level of T9. The xiphoid may remain cartilaginous until late in life; the linea alba and the sternal part of the diaphragm attach to it.

sk-89cf3635.stem: Which bone is the first to begin ossifying in the embryo?
sk-89cf3635.explanation: The clavicle begins to ossify in the 5th–6th week; its shaft ossifies in membrane (intramembranous) and its ends in cartilage. In adults it is one of the most frequently fractured bones.

sk-8791a2dc.stem: A child who fell off a bicycle has a clavicle fracture at the junction of its middle and lateral thirds. Which muscle pulls the medial fragment upwards?
sk-8791a2dc.explanation: In this fracture the medial fragment is pulled upwards by the clavicular head of sternocleidomastoid. The lateral fragment is pulled down by the weight of the arm and medially by pectoralis major and latissimus dorsi; the shoulder looks dropped and displaced forwards.
notes: It pulls the lateral fragment medially.
It attaches to the lateral fragment.
It attaches to the lateral third; it tries to hold the lateral fragment up but cannot overcome the weight of the arm.
It protects the subclavian vessels; it does not pull the fragment upwards.

sk-82483548.stem: Which structure passes beneath the superior transverse scapular ligament that bridges the suprascapular notch?
sk-82483548.explanation: The suprascapular nerve passes beneath the ligament and the suprascapular artery above it. Calcification of the ligament or entrapment in the notch causes weakness and wasting of supraspinatus and infraspinatus.

sk-4471bbd9.stem: Which of the following does NOT attach to the coracoid process?
sk-4471bbd9.explanation: The long head of biceps arises from the supraglenoid tubercle and runs within the joint capsule. Pectoralis minor, coracobrachialis, the short head of biceps and the coracoclavicular, coraco-acromial and coracohumeral ligaments attach to the coracoid process.

sk-5072fdb2.stem: An elderly woman who fell on her shoulder has a fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus. Flattening of the deltoid region and sensory loss in a small area on the outer shoulder develop. Which nerve is injured?
sk-5072fdb2.explanation: The axillary nerve passes with the posterior circumflex humeral artery through the quadrangular space and wraps around the back of the surgical neck. In a fracture, deltoid and teres minor weaken and sensation is lost over the 'regimental badge' area (superior lateral cutaneous nerve of the arm).

sk-70dfeb98.stem: After a fracture of the middle of the humeral shaft, a patient cannot lift the wrist and fingers (wrist drop). Which nerve and accompanying artery are injured at the fracture line?
options: Ulnar nerve – superior ulnar collateral artery
Axillary nerve – posterior circumflex humeral artery
sk-70dfeb98.explanation: The radial nerve and profunda brachii artery lie tightly against the bone in the radial groove on the back of the humerus. In shaft fractures the wrist and finger extensors are paralysed. Triceps is usually spared because its branches arise higher up.

sk-4c20df95.stem: A 7-year-old is brought in with a supracondylar humerus fracture after a fall. Hours later severe forearm pain, pain on passive finger extension and an absent radial pulse develop. Which vessel is damaged?
sk-4c20df95.explanation: In a supracondylar fracture the sharp end of the proximal fragment presses on the brachial artery and median nerve. The flexor compartment of the forearm becomes ischaemic; untreated, Volkmann's ischaemic contracture develops.

sk-7f0d202b.stem: Which nerve runs in the groove behind the medial epicondyle of the humerus?
options: Medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm
sk-7f0d202b.explanation: The ulnar nerve is superficial in the ulnar groove behind the medial epicondyle; the electric tingling into the hand when the elbow is knocked ('funny bone') comes from here. Entrapment in this region is called cubital tunnel syndrome.

sk-dd4258d5.stem: Which muscle attaches to the lesser tubercle of the humerus?
sk-dd4258d5.explanation: Of the rotator cuff muscles, supraspinatus, infraspinatus and teres minor attach to the greater tubercle; subscapularis alone attaches to the lesser tubercle and rotates the arm inwards.

sk-6cefc4df.stem: Which muscle attaches to the floor of the intertubercular sulcus?
sk-6cefc4df.explanation: Pectoralis major attaches to the lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus, teres major to the medial lip and latissimus dorsi to the floor ('a lady between two majors'). The groove contains the tendon of the long head of biceps and its synovial sheath.

sk-66af7b45.stem: A 2-year-old will not use the arm and holds the forearm pronated after the mother pulled sharply on the hand. Out of which ligament has the radial head slipped?
sk-66af7b45.explanation: 'Pulled elbow' (radial head subluxation) occurs in young children because the radial head is still small; the head slips out of the anular ligament that holds it against the radial notch of the ulna. It is easily reduced by supination and flexion.

sk-8eef6564.stem: An elderly woman who fell on her outstretched hand has a 'dinner fork' deformity of the wrist. X-ray shows a fracture of the distal radius with dorsal displacement of the distal fragment. What is this fracture called?
sk-8eef6564.explanation: In a Colles fracture the distal radial fragment is displaced dorsally and radially, giving a dinner-fork appearance from the side. A Smith fracture is the reverse (distal fragment volar). Monteggia is an ulna fracture with radial head dislocation; Galeazzi is a radius fracture with distal radio-ulnar dislocation.

sk-3a4562c9.stem: Which muscle attaches to the ulnar tuberosity?
sk-3a4562c9.explanation: Brachialis arises from the lower half of the front of the humerus and attaches to the coronoid process and ulnar tuberosity; it is the main flexor of the elbow. Biceps attaches to the radial tuberosity.
